root_cause.text: `get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()` in the hugetlb/memory-failure path dropped a folio reference with `folio_put()` while `hugetlb_lock` was still held, so if that put freed the hugetlb folio it re-entered `free_huge_folio()` and tried to take the same non-recursive lock, causing an AA self-deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `spin_lock_irq(&hugetlb_lock)` from the `mm/hugetlb.c` wrapper into `mm/memory-failure.c` and adds `spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock);` before `folio_put(folio)` at `out_unlock:`, matching the commit description that “The out: path in __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() calls folio_put() … while the hugetlb_lock is still held” and that `folio_put()` could trigger `free_huge_folio()` which “attempts to re-acquire the non-recursive hugetlb_lock.`

intent_record.intent_summary: Make hugetlb hwpoison page lookup self-contained by taking `hugetlb_lock` internally before folio validation.
intent_record.what: The function `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()` was renamed to `get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()` and changed from non-static to static. The comment stating it is called with `hugetlb_lock` held was removed. Inside the function, `struct folio *folio` is now declared without initialization, and `spin_lock_irq(&hugetlb_lock);` was added before `page_folio(page)` is called. A previous `goto out;` in the non-hugetlb case was changed to `goto out_unlock;`.
intent_record.how: The function now acquires `hugetlb_lock` itself before dereferencing the page into a folio, rather than relying on the caller to already hold the lock. This makes the hugetlb page validation and subsequent processing race-safe within the function and prevents use of `page_folio(page)` outside the intended lock coverage. The updated unlock label indicates the function now manages lock release on its own error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the hugetlb hwpoison path to use the proper unlock cleanup label on early returns.
intent_record.what: The two error/early-exit paths in `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()` were changed to jump to `out_unlock` instead of `out` when `MF_NO_RETRY` is not set and when `hugetlb_update_hwpoison()` returns `>= MF_HUGETLB_FOLIO_PRE_POISONED`.
intent_record.how: This changes the cleanup path taken on these exits so the function now releases the lock/resource handled by `out_unlock` before returning, preventing a premature exit that would skip required unlocking or equivalent cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure `hugetlb_lock` is always unlocked before returning from `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()`.
intent_record.what: The function now calls `spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock);` immediately before the normal `return ret;`, and the old `out:` label was renamed to `out_unlock:` with an added `spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock);` before the optional `folio_put(folio);` cleanup and final return.
intent_record.how: This change ensures the `hugetlb_lock` spinlock is released on both the success path and the cleanup/error path before exiting the function, preventing the lock from remaining held and avoiding deadlock or lock misuse at runtime.

candidates.rationale: This wrapper acquires hugetlb_lock around the hwpoison helper, which is the lock that became implicated in the self-deadlock when the helper path later dropped a folio reference and re-entered hugetlb folio free handling.

Dropping the folio reference here while hugetlb_lock was still held is the direct trigger described in the root cause: if this put frees the hugetlb folio, it can recurse into free_huge_folio() and deadlock on the same lock.

This return occurs before the cleanup path that releases the folio reference/lock state, making it part of the buggy control flow where the helper can exit without ensuring the lock is dropped before folio release.
